messages.text:
**Daily Market Summary · 13 November 2026**
**Alert**
• BTC fell below $70,000: price is now about $68,799, right on its 200-week average ($68,118), the last big floor.
• BTC broke below its 30-day low ($71,460): the month-long slide has made a new low.
• Headline label changed from BULLISH to NEUTRAL: the headline now reads the last month or two, which is mixed; the long-term trend is still up.
• Fear & Greed fell into extreme fear (20).
**Snapshot**
• Bitcoin about $68,799, down about 9.3% in 7 days. Headline NEUTRAL, low confidence. Fear & Greed 20 (extreme fear).
• Price has closed under its 50-day average for 23 days and is about 6% under its 200-day average.
**What happened (last 24h)**
• Bitcoin fell below $69,000 (PANews); no single cause is reported beyond the broad tech-stock drop after Nvidia's CEO stepped down.
• About $1.23 billion of bets on a rise were forced to close in 24 hours (PANews).
**Short-term outlook (next 1-7 days)**
• Lean: soft to neutral, the mood is very fearful.
• Turns up: a close above $70,750 (top of a typical week's swing), then $73,044 (200-day average).
• Sideways: $68,118 to $70,750; a normal week swings about $4,069.
• Turns down: a close below $68,118 (200-week average), then $62,819 (90-day low).
• Rally watch: drop window open; a rally signal needs about $81,912, a fresh drop signal comes below about $69,776.
• Next scheduled event: Fed meeting on 8 December.
**News that matters**
• US DOJ froze about $2.7 billion stolen from Binance; Binance says affected assets are covered (Bloomberg via PANews): short term, small positive.
• Nvidia CEO stepped down, tech and crypto-related stocks fell (PANews): short term, small negative.
• US Treasury plans bank-style checks on stablecoin issuers (PANews): medium term, small negative.
**Altcoins & themes**
• The tech-stock shock is weighing on the big coins: ETH about -6% and SOL about -6% in 24h (CoinGecko).
• Babylon (BABY, Baru on Reku): the project says Aave's community voted to accept native Bitcoin as collateral through Babylon.
**Bigger picture**
• Next month is mixed and 3-6 months still leans up but weaker; a close back above $73,044 (200-day average) would put the recovery back on track, closes below $68,118 would weaken it.
https://andrifa.github.io/crypto-market-state-dashboard/

**Paid:** hold trader-targeted spend and keep a reserve while the drop window is open and Bitcoin tests its 200-week average ($68,118). Apply the d30 ROI stop-loss to running campaigns. Do not step up trader spend until a close back above $73,044 (200-day average); keep rally creatives ready in case a rally signal comes near $81,912.

**Social:** keep the normal rhythm with calm, factual posts. Explain why crypto fell with tech stocks after Nvidia's CEO stepped down (PANews), and add a plain explainer on why about $1.23 billion of borrowed-money bets were forced to close in a day. The DOJ freeze of $2.7 billion stolen from Binance (Bloomberg via PANews) is a good trust story.

**CRM:** send existing holders a calm note that Bitcoin is about 16% lower over the month and testing its 200-week average, with an explainer link and no push to trade. Add a security reminder on fake wallet letters (PANews on the SafePal phishing scam). Keep lifecycle journeys, pause deposit promotions.

**SEO:** refresh 'why is Bitcoin down' and 'Bitcoin price today': likely to draw searches because Bitcoin fell under $69,000; Pintu and Pluang are both covering the drop. Publish or refresh a 'December Fed meeting and crypto' explainer ahead of 8 December (Pintu has one), and the tokenized stocks guide (Pintu and Pluang covered it). Check against Reku's pages. https://andrifa.github.io/crypto-market-state-dashboard/

**Altcoins:** the tech-stock shock is the main theme; ETH and SOL are both about 6% lower in 24h (CoinGecko), and PANews gives no single cause beyond the broad drop. Binance-linked news: the US DOJ froze about $2.7 billion stolen from Binance (Bloomberg via PANews). On Reku's new listings, Babylon (BABY) says Aave's community voted to accept native Bitcoin as collateral through its vaults, according to the project and PANews.
